steps.say: The revised FIGO 2018 staging system for cervical cancer fundamentally changed clinical oncology practice by allowing cross-sectional imaging and pathological evaluation to allocate final stage. This modern framework integrates pelvic magnetic resonance imaging, computed tomography, and positron emission tomography alongside operative surgical pathology.
steps.tx: The updated **FIGO 2018 staging** system for cervical cancer formally integrates **cross-sectional imaging** modalities such as MRI, CT, and PET-CT and surgical pathological findings alongside clinical examination to assign definitive clinical and pathological stage groupings across early and advanced neoplasms.  Evidence-based practice integrates imaging incorporation, pathological staging.

nodes.label: Document invasive cervical cancer on biopsy
Acquire pelvic MRI for local tumor dimension
Perform whole-body PET-CT for nodal spread

steps.say: Microinvasive cervical carcinoma is designated as Stage IA and is diagnosed exclusively through microscopic examination of an excisional cone biopsy. The maximum depth of stromal invasion is five millimeters or less, and horizontal surface dimension has been eliminated from the staging definition.
steps.tx: **Stage IA** microinvasive carcinoma is diagnosed exclusively by microscopic tissue assessment of excisional specimens. **Stage IA1** denotes measured stromal invasion <=3 mm, while **Stage IA2** denotes stromal invasion >3 mm and <=5 mm, with lateral dimension criteria omitted from the current classification schema.  Evidence-based practice integrates stromal invasion >3 to <=5 mm. Key numerical parameters include 2018.

left.title: Stage IA1 Carcinoma
points: Conization alone with clear margins curative

steps.say: Stage IB comprises invasive carcinoma strictly confined to the cervix with stromal invasion depth exceeding five millimeters. FIGO 2018 subdivided this stage into three discrete categories based on maximum clinical tumor dimension measured on imaging or gross examination.
steps.tx: **Stage IB** denotes clinically visible or invasive lesion >5 mm stromal depth confined to the uterine cervix: **Stage IB1** measures >=5 mm depth and <2 cm dimension; **Stage IB2** measures >=2 cm and <4 cm; and **Stage IB3** measures >=4 cm largest dimension.  Evidence-based practice integrates 2 cm cutoff, 4 cm cutoff.

rows: Type C radical hysterectomy with lymphadenectomy

steps.say: Stage II tumor extends directly beyond the uterus into adjacent soft tissues but without extending to the pelvic sidewall or lower third of the vagina. Substage IIA involves the upper two-thirds of the vagina, while substage IIB demonstrates parametrial infiltration.
steps.tx: **Stage II** cervical cancer extends beyond the cervix: **Stage IIA1** involves upper two-thirds of vagina <4 cm; **Stage IIA2** involves upper vagina >=4 cm without parametrial invasion; and **Stage IIB** exhibits distinct **parametrial invasion** sparing the pelvic sidewall and lower vaginal third completely.

left.title: Stage IIA Disease
points: IIA1 <4 cm operable; IIA2 >=4 cm CCRT

right.title: Stage IIB Disease
points: Does not reach bony pelvic sidewall

steps.say: A signature innovation of the 2018 system is the creation of Stage IIIC for lymph node metastases confirmed by either radiological imaging or pathological dissection. Pelvic nodal involvement designates IIIC1, whereas para-aortic nodal metastasis designates IIIC2.
steps.tx: **Stage IIIC** explicitly reflects nodal spread confirmed radiologically (designated r) or pathologically (designated p). **Stage IIIC1** identifies pelvic lymph node metastasis only, whereas **Stage IIIC2** identifies **para-aortic lymph node** metastasis irrespective of primary cervical tumor size or local pelvic extent.  Evidence-based practice integrates pelvic lymph nodes. Key numerical parameters include 3.

nodes.label: Evaluate retroperitoneal lymph nodes on imaging/pathology

steps.say: High-resolution pelvic magnetic resonance imaging serves as the premier diagnostic imaging modality for assessing primary cervical tumors. T2-weighted MRI provides diagnostic accuracy exceeding ninety percent for cervical stromal invasion depth and parametrial infiltration.
steps.tx: Pelvic **magnetic resonance imaging** is the gold-standard imaging modality for local tumor assessment. High-resolution T2-weighted MRI delivers >90% accuracy for measuring **stromal invasion depth**, endocervical canal extent, **parametrial infiltration**, and subtle vaginal fornix extension prior to definitive therapy planning.  Evidence-based practice integrates pelvic MRI, parametrial infiltration accuracy, local tumor staging.

rows: Spiculated soft tissue in parametrial fat
Loss of hypointense vaginal wall stripe

steps.say: Whole-body FDG PET-CT offers superior diagnostic sensitivity and specificity for identifying occult pelvic and distant retroperitoneal nodal metastases. PET-CT staging is strongly recommended for all tumors measuring two centimeters or larger to guide radiation portal design.
steps.tx: Whole-body **18F-FDG PET-CT** demonstrates 85% to 90% sensitivity and >95% specificity for detecting pelvic and retroperitoneal **nodal metastases**. Routine PET-CT evaluation is strongly recommended in tumors >=IB2 to avoid missing occult para-aortic metastasis that alters the radiotherapy field.  Evidence-based practice integrates para-aortic nodal sensitivity, distant metastases.

left.title: Pelvic MRI Utility
points: Accurate local measurement of tumor size
Optimal for parametrial and vaginal invasion

steps.say: Stage IV represents advanced dissemination beyond the true pelvis or into adjacent mucosal organs. Biopsy-proven invasion into the mucosal lining of the bladder or rectum defines Stage IVA, whereas distant haematogenous or extrapelvic lymphatic spread defines Stage IVB.
steps.tx: **Stage IVA** requires biopsy-proven invasion through the mucosal lining of bladder or rectum; bullous edema alone does not qualify. **Stage IVB** identifies **distant metastasis** or hematogenous dissemination to lungs, liver, peritoneal cavity, or distant supraclavicular lymph node basins.  Evidence-based practice integrates mucosal invasion bladder rectum, bullous edema insufficient. Key numerical parameters include 4.

nodes.label: Suspicion of adjacent organ or distant invasion
Cystoscopy and proctoscopy with mucosal biopsy
Mucosal biopsy positive: assign Stage IVA
PET-CT shows lung, liver, or distant nodal spread
Distant metastases confirmed: assign Stage IVB
